# Action

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask docs generate` from `schemas/policy/v1.json`. Do not edit by hand. -->

The action of a rule (#34).

Each action is an object with a `type`, and its options as optional
keys, so options can be added later without a breaking change.

Appears at: `/rule_sets/rules/action`.

## Variants

### `type: allow`

Permit execution.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Constraints | Since | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | constant | yes |  | always `"allow"` | 1.0.0 |  |

### `type: deny`

Block execution.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Constraints | Since | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `allow_request` | boolean | no |  |  | 1.0.0 | The end user may raise an approval request (#11). Needs a notification, and is not valid in a mandatory rule set. |
| `kill_running` | boolean | no |  |  | 1.0.0 | Terminate already-running instances that match when the policy is applied. Not valid for drivers or libraries. |
| `on_unparseable` | [`UnknownAs`](types.md#unknownas) | no |  |  | 1.0.0 | Whether a version fact that is not a version counts towards the rule applying (#32, #35). With `match`, each version criterion on such a fact is taken in whichever direction makes the deny apply, also under `not`. The rest of the tree is evaluated as usual. `no_match`, the default, leaves the criterion `Unknown`, which `unknown_as` then decides. |
| `request_template` | [`RequestTemplateRef`](types.md#requesttemplateref) | no |  |  | 1.0.0 | The approval request template to use. Only with `allow_request`. |
| `type` | constant | yes |  | always `"deny"` | 1.0.0 |  |
| `unknown_as` | [`UnknownAs`](types.md#unknownas) | no |  |  | 1.0.0 | Whether the rule blocks when its match tree is `Unknown` because a fact is missing or cannot be trusted (#32, #35). `no_match`, the default, means an unknown fact does not block; `match` makes the deny fail closed. |

### `type: audit`

Record the match without changing the outcome. A non-terminal
annotation, used for detection and tagging.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Constraints | Since | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | constant | yes |  | always `"audit"` | 1.0.0 |  |

### `type: allow_contained`

Permit execution inside a containment profile (#14). The engine only
carries the reference.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Constraints | Since | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `profile_id` | [`ContainmentProfileRef`](types.md#containmentprofileref) | yes |  |  | 1.0.0 | The containment profile the process runs under. |
| `type` | constant | yes |  | always `"allow_contained"` | 1.0.0 |  |

### `type: allow_elevated`

Permit execution with an elevated token (#12). The engine only
carries the directive.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Constraints | Since | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `auth` | [`ElevationAuth`](types.md#elevationauth) | no |  |  | 1.0.0 | What the user must do to confirm. |
| `condition` | [`ElevationCondition`](types.md#elevationcondition) | yes |  |  | 1.0.0 | When to elevate. |
| `reason_prompt` | string | no |  | 1 to 256 characters | 1.0.0 | If set, the user must give a reason, and this is the prompt shown: one line of 1 to 256 characters, trimmed, with no control characters (including tab and line breaks) and no bidirectional formatting characters, so the prompt cannot be made to read differently. |
| `token_profile` | [`TokenProfileRef`](types.md#tokenprofileref) | yes |  |  | 1.0.0 | The access token profile to build the token from. |
| `type` | constant | yes |  | always `"allow_elevated"` | 1.0.0 |  |

### `type: trust_source`

Mark the matching process as a trusted installer, updater or source
(#9, #114). This does not permit the process itself to run; an allow
rule decides that. The engine returns the directive.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Constraints | Since | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | [`TrustMode`](types.md#trustmode) | yes |  |  | 1.0.0 | Which writes are trusted. |
| `scope_paths` | array of string | yes |  | 1 to 32 items | 1.0.0 | The folders whose new content becomes trusted: 1 to 32 absolute paths (`C:\...`, `\\server\share\...`, or a known path variable such as `%PROGRAMFILES%\...`), each at most 1024 bytes, written with `\`, and unique (compared as the engine compares paths). |
| `tag_output` | boolean | no |  |  | 1.0.0 | Tag the files written with a persistent trust claim, so they stay trusted after the process exits. Off by default. |
| `type` | constant | yes |  | always `"trust_source"` | 1.0.0 |  |

### `type: ignore`

Skip the object entirely: no decision is logged. Only for performance
exclusions, never for executables or drivers, and validation always
warns.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Constraints | Since | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | constant | yes |  | always `"ignore"` | 1.0.0 |  |

### `type: defer`

No opinion. A first-match model continues with the next rule (#35).

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Constraints | Since | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | constant | yes |  | always `"defer"` | 1.0.0 |  |
